name: Green River
reach: Flaming Gorge Dam to Gates of Lodore
agency: USFS Ashley National Forest / BLM Vernal Field Office

camps.name: Little Hole camps
camps.desc: Designated riverside camps on the lower Little Hole trail. Camping and fires are not allowed on the upper trail.

camps.name: Cottonwood
camps.desc: Foot access along the trail. A vault toilet is nearby.

camps.name: Red Creek I & II
camps.desc: Boat access only. A vault toilet is nearby.

camps.name: Indian Crossing
camps.desc: BLM fee campground with ramp, drinking water, toilets and dump station.

camps.name: Taylor Flat
camps.desc: A cottonwood camp above Indian Crossing, once heavily used.

camps.name: Bridge Hollow Campground
camps.desc: A BLM fee campground about 400 yards below Indian Crossing, beside the John Jarvie Ranch. Water, toilets, boat ramp and credit card phone.

camps.name: Little Swallow
camps.desc: A sandy camp directly below Little Swallow Rapid.

camps.name: Swinging Bridge Campground
camps.desc: Browns Park National Wildlife Refuge. Free, no potable water, no direct river access.

camps.name: Crook Campground
camps.desc: Browns Park National Wildlife Refuge. Free, no potable water, no direct river access.

rapids.name: First Anticipation
rapids.desc: The first of the Section A rapids below the dam.

rapids.name: Mother-in-Law
rapids.desc: The most difficult rapid in Section A, with a sign on the right before it. Reaches Class III at some flows.

rapids.name: Red Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: The biggest rapid on the run, short and easy to scout. At low flow there are two channels: the right carries most of the water, with holes near the top, two large boulders to avoid and a boulder garden at the exit; the left is shallower and straighter. Red Creek can muddy the river after rain.

rapids.name: Taylor Flat Bridge
rapids.desc: A low bridge, impassable at 4,500 cfs or higher. Take out before it at Indian Crossing or Bridge Hollow.

rapids.name: Splashy water below the bridge
rapids.desc: A short splashy section just past Taylor Flat Bridge.

rapids.name: Little Swallow
rapids.desc: The last rapid in Section C, fun and splashy. A sandy camp sits directly below.

hikes.name: Little Hole National Recreation Trail
hikes.desc: Follows the river along all of Section A, from the dam to Little Hole. High flows wash out sections of its boardwalk.

hikes.name: John Jarvie Ranch
hikes.desc: A historic BLM ranch beside Bridge Hollow Campground. Guided tours by arrangement with the Vernal Field Office (435-781-4400).

rules.d: Carry a bail bucket, a throw line and an extra oar. Life jackets must be worn on the water.
A portable toilet system is required for all campers.
Motors are not allowed in the float-in camp section.
Obtain firewood near your destination and burn it on site to prevent the spread of tree-killing pests.
Flows fluctuate daily, roughly from 830 to 4,500 cfs depending on dam releases. The river can drop sharply overnight and strand a boat left floating at the beach.
Reclamation runs at least two weeks of high flow each year, up to about 8,600 cfs, for June sucker spawning.
Taylor Flat Bridge, below Indian Crossing, cannot be passed at 4,500 cfs or higher.
Section A and B hold a heavy trout fishery. Let commercial and fishing groups pass in the narrow stretches.
Flaming Gorge Resort and Dutch John Resort run shuttles to the dam and pickups at Little Hole or Indian Crossing.

landmarks.name: Spillway boat launch
landmarks.desc: Section A put-in below the dam. A day-use fee applies, with a steep staircase from the parking area to the ramp and a busy commercial fishing fleet.

landmarks.name: Little Hole
landmarks.desc: End of Section A. Three boat ramps, restrooms and picnic tables. About 90 percent of the traffic drops off below here.

landmarks.name: Indian Crossing
landmarks.desc: End of Section B. A BLM fee area with a boat ramp, drinking water, toilets and a dump station.

landmarks.name: Taylor Flat Bridge
landmarks.desc: A low bridge just below Indian Crossing. Signs warn that it cannot be floated at extreme high water.

landmarks.name: Bridge Hollow Campground
landmarks.desc: A fee campground with a boat ramp, water and toilets, about 400 yards below Indian Crossing.

landmarks.name: Swallow Canyon
landmarks.desc: An optional take-out on Browns Park Road, 25 or more miles from the dam.

landmarks.name: Swinging Bridge
landmarks.desc: A take-out in Colorado at Browns Park National Wildlife Refuge, about 3 to 4 miles past Swallow Canyon.

landmarks.name: Crook Campground
landmarks.desc: Browns Park National Wildlife Refuge campground.

landmarks.name: Gates of Lodore
landmarks.desc: Take-out at the head of Lodore Canyon in Dinosaur National Monument; a free permit from the monument is required to go on.

access.name: Spillway
access.note: Section A put-in below the dam

permit.status: No permit to float · float-in camps reserved on Recreation.gov

items.d: No permit is required for private floating from Flaming Gorge Dam to the Dinosaur National Monument boundary at Lodore. Permits are required for commercial float boating only.
Continuing into Lodore Canyon requires a permit from Dinosaur National Monument.
A Recreational Use Pass is required for the float-in sites, which lie in the Flaming Gorge National Recreation Area.
The 17 float-in camps between Little Hole and Browns Park are reserved in advance on Recreation.gov or at the Little Hole boat ramp, and can be reached only on foot or by boat.
No camping is allowed in Section A.
A picnic table, a fire ring with benches, tent pads and a blind for a portable toilet. Vault toilets are near Cottonwood and Red Creek. There is no potable water.
